name: Utopia predictable airdrop balance overwrite
summary: Utopia._airdrop overwrites rather than increments a predictably chosen address balance. A crafted pair skim overwrote the pair’s Utopia balance, allowing sync and tiny subsequent sales to drain WBNB reserves.

loss.notes: WBNB extracted from pair 0xfeef619a56fce9d003e20bf61393d18f62b0b2d5: 492.088605739133158123 in the anchor plus six later payouts totaling 3.657063239971340118, less the attacker’s 0.01 WBNB purchase input. Protocol fee conversions retained as MT for LP rewards are excluded. No separate value is assigned to overwritten or unsold Utopia balances; gas and subsequent transfers do not reduce gross loss. WBNB is valued at the timestamped BNB/USD sample.

ageReset.description: startTrade enables the arbitrary-recipient pair transfer that makes the chosen balance overwrite possible; before activation the !Trade gate permits only liquidity additions to the fixed mainPair.

sources.note: Reviewed creation receipt/trace, exploit call trace, and verified source at https://bscscan.com/address/0xb1da08c472567eb0ec19639b1822f578d39f3333#code. The token executes directly; no delegatecall, upgrade, or selfdestruct path exists. Runtime is absent at block 25944622 and hashes identically at deployment, trading activation, and pre-exploit block 30119396. startTradeBlock changes from zero to 25945528 in source-4, remains that value before exploitation, and its sole setter requires zero. Before activation, non-whitelisted transfers must be liquidity additions to mainPair; the arbitrary-recipient skim transfer used for targeted overwrite reverts. Activation removes that restriction. The main pair is marked as a swap pair at construction and remains non-whitelisted at activation and pre-exploit. Complete direct token history through block 30120000 contains no whitelist or swap-pair setters. The three privileged external addresses fixed at construction have no code at deployment/pre-exploit; other whitelist members are the token, fixed router, distributor, zero and dead addresses, whose available call paths cannot change these settings. Fee/reward accounting and liquidity size do not establish the overwrite defect. The standard pair merely consumes the token’s corrupted balance and is not a separate defect-bearing target.

Reviewed successful anchor and all campaign receipts, attacker transaction history, indexed overwrite logs, and the first later sale trace. The anchor is the attacker’s nonce-zero transaction. Transfer(pair,pair,1) at log 71 witnesses the balance assignment; sync at log 74 reports zero Utopia reserve, then log 77 reports one raw unit, followed by the WBNB drain at log 80. The complete matching pair-overwrite log query from deployment through block 121409061 returns only this transaction. Subsequent helper deployments do not exercise the overwrite; the later helper swap reverts. Source-5 first transfers 0.033971157951470846 retained Utopia to the attacker, then records sales of 50, 50, 100, 200, 2000 and 4000 raw units from that inventory. Their direct attacker WBNB payouts are respectively 1.973546337429242189, 0.233213908808913388, 0.260301827986355250, 0.344473271475718246, 0.650807952379615620 and 0.194719941891495425. Automatic fee swaps route WBNB through USDT into MT returned to Utopia for LP rewards, not to the attacker, and are excluded. The quantity measures realised WBNB extraction, excluding the identifiable purchase input, without pricing Utopia at corrupted reserves. Source-6 returns BNB/USD 241.98 at timestamp 1689830564; WBNB unwraps one-for-one. Later attacker history contains withdrawals and onward transfers, not additional pool extraction.
